title: New Year: the Holy Name
hook: on the eighth day he was named Jesus; Catholics also honor Mary, Mother of God

segments.voice: Yesterday, Herod, and Rachel weeping in Bethlehem, her grief allowed to stand. Your line was rachel weeping.

The countdown hits zero, the fireworks go up, and the year turns over. By morning, the new calendar is on the wall with every square still empty. People make resolutions. Some pick a word for the year. The church calendar marks this same day with something older and simpler: a baby being given his name. Count from Christmas, and New Year's Day falls on the eighth day, the day a Jewish boy was circumcised and named. So, in many churches, the calendar year opens with a name.

Luke gives it one verse. In the King James Bible: "And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb." Two things stand out. Mary and Joseph keep the law of their people: Jesus is circumcised and named like any Jewish boy. And they don't choose the name; it was given before he was conceived. Matthew's Gospel says why, in the angel's words to Joseph: "and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins." Matthew hears in the name what the child would do. Paul writes to the Philippians that God has "given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow." Churches keep this day in different ways. Anglicans and Lutherans keep the Naming and Circumcision of Jesus, or the Holy Name. Orthodox Christians keep the Circumcision of the Lord, along with the memory of St Basil. Catholics keep the feast of Mary, Mother of God, honoring the one who carried the child, and they honor the Holy Name in these early days of January too. In the Orthodox world, a short prayer is built around this name, the Jesus Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me. Some pray it slowly, with the breath. The church's own year began weeks ago, with Advent. But on the first of January, in many churches, the calendar year starts not with a resolution but with a name, said quietly.

segments.voice: Let your breathing slow. If you pray, you can say the name of Jesus quietly on the out-breath, or the Jesus Prayer a line at a time: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me. If that isn't your practice, choose one word to carry into the year and say it inside on each breath, and let the empty calendar wait.
New Year. In the church's calendar, the eighth day after Christmas, when the child was circumcised and named Jesus, and when Catholics honor Mary, Mother of God.
Your line: his name was jesus. The year opens with a name. Day one thousand fourteen.

chat.says: Why do some churches celebrate Jesus's name on New Year's Day?
options: It's the eighth day after Christmas, when Luke says the child was circumcised and named.
It's the day Jesus was baptized, when the voice from heaven gave him his name.
Because Mary and Joseph chose his name on the first day of the new year.

Editor: 'given before he existed' changed to Luke's 'before he was conceived' (the old line clashed with Christian teaching); dropped 'and named' for Mary, since Luke 2:21 doesn't say who named him.
Editor 2: added a comma to the hook's counting line so it reads cleanly aloud.

Audit: hook and teach called 1 January 'the church's new year'; the Western liturgical year begins at Advent (and the Byzantine church year on 1 September). Now 'the calendar year', with a line noting the church's own year began at Advent.
